source_metadata.title: Candida Colonization in the Respiratory Tract: What Is the Significance?

atoms.canonical_statement: This opinion article examines the clinical significance of Candida respiratory-tract colonization in critically ill patients, including its potential relationships with ventilator-associated pneumonia, bacterial colonization, and antibacterial resistance.
The article reports an approximately 15% Candida spp. isolation rate among hospitalized patients undergoing active screening.

population.label: Hospitalized patients undergoing active Candida screening

atoms.canonical_statement: The article reports that Candida spp. isolation by active screening can be as high as 25% in critically ill patients.

population.label: Critically ill patients undergoing active Candida screening

atoms.canonical_statement: The article states that respiratory-tract isolation of Candida usually represents colonization and that anti-Candida therapy is rarely necessary in most such cases.

Unlike bacterial VAP, for which quantitative culture cutoffs are described, no diagnostic quantitative threshold has been established for Candida; the article states that Candida pneumonia requires histopathologic diagnosis.
The article reports that IDSA and ESCMID guidance does not recommend antifungal treatment for respiratory Candida isolation unless there is clear histologic evidence of infection.
In a cited autopsy study of 135 patients who died of pneumonia, 77 (57%) had Candida airway colonization during hospitalization, but zero cases were pathologically confirmed as Candida pneumonia.

population.label: Patients who died of pneumonia in the cited autopsy study

exposures.details: 77 of 135 patients (57%) were reported as colonized

atoms.canonical_statement: A cited controlled before-after microbiology laboratory study reported antifungal treatment in 21% of patients under limited respiratory yeast identification versus 39% under full identification (p < 0.05).

population.label: Patients in the cited controlled before-after respiratory microbiology reporting study

concept.text: Limited respiratory secretion identification (filamentous fungi reported)

atoms.canonical_statement: The same cited controlled before-after study reported hospital length of stay of 10.1 days with limited respiratory yeast identification versus 12.1 days with full identification (p < 0.05).

population.label: Patients in the cited controlled before-after respiratory microbiology reporting study

concept.text: Limited respiratory secretion identification (filamentous fungi reported)

atoms.canonical_statement: The article reports that Candida beta-glucan can impair alveolar macrophage and neutrophil function and reduce reactive oxygen species production.
A cited rat study is reported to have found that Candida-associated inflammatory responses inhibited alveolar macrophage phagocytosis and increased Pseudomonas aeruginosa airway colonization.

The article reports experimental evidence that Candida colonization can facilitate colonization by Staphylococcus aureus and Enterobacteriaceae and can be associated with increased bacterial pneumonia.
Candida biofilms are described as protecting Candida while strongly adsorbing co-existing bacteria, with adherent polymicrobial structures that are difficult to remove.
The article reports animal evidence suggesting that Candida albicans can protect co-inoculated bacteria from clearance by normal alveolar macrophages.
A cited animal experiment is reported to have found greater alveolar invasiveness of Acinetobacter baumannii pneumonia in mice with Candida colonization.
The article reports that Staphylococcus aureus can form microcolonies within Candida albicans polymicrobial biofilms and that this configuration can increase vancomycin resistance.

The article reports identification of 27 Staphylococcus aureus-specific proteins in polymicrobial biofilm conditions, including changes linked to oxidative-stress resistance, antibiotic resistance, and downregulation of the virulence regulator CodY.

Figure 1 depicts a proposed interaction in mechanically ventilated patients in which Candida biofilms protect Candida, adsorb co-existing bacteria, and may contribute to multidrug-resistant bacterial isolation through resistance-plasmid transmission and polymicrobial biofilm formation.
The article reports that Candida respiratory-tract isolation rates in mechanically ventilated ICU patients can be as high as 50%.

population.label: Mechanically ventilated ICU patients in cited clinical studies

atoms.canonical_statement: A cited clinical study reported a median hospital stay of 59.9 days in patients with Candida respiratory-tract colonization versus 38.6 days in those without colonization (p = 0.006).

population.label: Mechanically ventilated ICU patients in the cited clinical study

atoms.canonical_statement: A cited clinical study reported hospital mortality of 34.2% in patients with Candida respiratory-tract colonization versus 21.0% in those without colonization (p = 0.003).

population.label: Mechanically ventilated ICU patients in the cited clinical study

atoms.canonical_statement: A cited prospective cohort reported Pseudomonas aeruginosa VAP incidence of 9% with Candida respiratory-tract colonization versus 4.8% without colonization (p = 0.048).

population.label: Patients in the cited prospective cohort

atoms.canonical_statement: The cited prospective cohort is reported to have identified Candida respiratory-tract colonization as an independent risk factor for Pseudomonas aeruginosa VAP.

A cited single-center retrospective case-control study is reported to have suggested that antifungal therapy in patients with Candida albicans airway colonization could prevent Pseudomonas aeruginosa VAP.
A cited cohort study is reported to have found that inhaled amphotericin B reduced Candida airway burden in mechanically ventilated patients but did not reduce VAP morbidity or ICU mortality.

The article reports that the EMPIRICUS randomized trial did not show a decrease in VAP incidence or 28-day mortality with micafungin versus placebo; the article gives 32% versus 39.8% with p > 0.05 but does not unambiguously tie those values to a single named endpoint.

In the FUNGIBACT prospective cohort of 146 patients mechanically ventilated for more than 96 hours, Candida airway colonization was not associated with bacterial VAP after adjustment for mHLA-DR (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.59-1.65; p = 0.95).

population.label: FUNGIBACT patients mechanically ventilated for more than 96 hours

atoms.canonical_statement: In a cited retrospective study of 269 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and hospital-acquired pneumonia, 186 patients (69.1%) had Candida airway colonization.

population.label: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and hospital-acquired pneumonia

atoms.canonical_statement: In the cited systemic lupus erythematosus cohort, multidrug-resistant bacteria were detected in 58.6% of Candida-colonized patients versus 36.1% of non-colonized patients (p < 0.001).

population.label: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and hospital-acquired pneumonia

atoms.canonical_statement: The cited systemic lupus erythematosus study is reported to have found faster normalization of secreted IgA and IL-17 after antifungal treatment.
The cited systemic lupus erythematosus study reported no significant effect on 28-day mortality, with values of 14.5 versus 10.8 and p > 0.05.
The cited meta-analysis of Candida airway colonization and outcomes in VAP included four prospective studies, three retrospective studies, and one cross-sectional study.
The cited meta-analysis reported longer durations of mechanical ventilation among patients with Candida airway colonization.
The cited meta-analysis reported higher 28-day mortality with Candida airway colonization (RR 1.64, 95% CI 1.27-2.12).

population.label: Patients with VAP included across the cited meta-analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: The cited meta-analysis reported higher ICU mortality with Candida airway colonization (RR 1.57, 95% CI 1.26-1.94).

population.label: Patients with VAP included across the cited meta-analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: The article notes that attributable mortality was difficult to determine in the cited studies because of confounding and insufficient sample size.

The article notes substantial baseline heterogeneity across studies, including differences in reasons for mechanical ventilation, VAP severity, antibiotic exposure before VAP diagnosis, and immune status.

The authors conclude that Candida pneumonia is rarely confirmed, Candida airway colonization may influence bacterial colonization and resistance, current clinical findings are inconsistent, and further studies are needed to evaluate pre-emptive antifungal therapy for VAP prevention.
The authors declared no commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.
The article states that supplementary material is available online through the Frontiers article page.

extraction_limitations: The governing atom workflow is designed for primary literature, but this source is explicitly an Opinion article. Numerical and study-specific claims summarized from cited literature are tagged secondary_report and should be verified against the cited primary study or meta-analysis before being treated as primary-source evidence.

The PDF contains Figure 1, which was visually inspected and represented as a figure-anchored atom. Supplementary Figure 1 and Supplementary Table 1 are referenced but are not contained in the uploaded five-page PDF and were not extracted.

The EMPIRICUS paragraph reports 32% versus 39.8% with p > 0.05 while discussing both VAP incidence and 28-day mortality; because the uploaded source does not unambiguously map that pair to one endpoint, the claim was retained as a qualitative atom with an ambiguity tag rather than normalized into a quantitative endpoint.
The systemic-lupus cohort reports 28-day mortality as 14.5 versus 10.8 with p > 0.05 without an explicit percent sign in the sentence; the values were not assigned a unit.
No study-level details absent from the Opinion article were imported from the reference list or external sources.
